_notes.taxonomy_source: Categories mirror the Pitts Ads dataset (Hussain et al., CVPR 2017) and the AdsQA benchmark (arXiv 2509.08621). We use four categories — kept deliberately small so the experiment has at least 3 ads per category and the factor 'ad category' is analytically tractable.
_notes.url_status: All ad creatives are synthetic MP4s in static/ads/, generated by scripts/generate_ads_v3.py. Each advertises a fictitious product; the content genre it belongs to is conveyed by the ad's graphics and mood, never named in its copy.
_notes.how_to_use_in_ads_slots: Each entry in experiment.json's ads array can either inline the legacy fields (url, placement, etc.) or set library_ref to one of the ids below; the player resolves library_ref before scheduling. See app.py::resolve_ad().

categories.label: Thrill Seeker
categories.description: Action, adventure, horror and sports content. Relevant ads: rollercoaster-park tickets, energy drink, running shoes, climbing gear.

categories.label: Intellectual Explorer
categories.description: Sci-fi, fantasy, science and technology content. Relevant ads: smartphone, 3D animation software, home telescope, VR headset.

categories.label: Content Chameleon
categories.description: Comedy, family, musicals and animation content. Relevant ads: popcorn, breakfast cereal, karaoke machine, theatre tickets.

categories.label: Investigative Viewer
categories.description: Crime, film noir, thrillers and courtroom content. Relevant ads: smart doorbell camera, legal-advice app, detective audiobooks, crime-fiction magazine.
